subject: Business
title: Total Cost of Ownership
description: A quick, practical guide to Total Cost of Ownership.

hook.text: The cheapest bid won the contract. Then quality issues, delays, and rework tripled the actual cost.

buildup.text: Total cost of ownership (TCO) includes not just the purchase price but shipping, quality, risk, and support costs.

discovery.text: A supplier 15% cheaper with 5% defect rate may cost more than one 15% pricier with 0.1% defects.

twist.text: Most procurement teams are rewarded for purchase price, not TCO. The incentive drives bad decisions.

climax.text: Toyota evaluates suppliers on quality, delivery, flexibility, and continuous improvement — not just price.

punchline.text: The cheapest bid is often the most expensive choice.

quiz.question: What does Total Cost of Ownership include?
options: Purchase price plus shipping, quality, risk, and support costs
Only the warranty and service costs

details.summary: Total cost of ownership calculates the complete lifecycle cost of a purchase beyond just the unit price, including transportation, storage, quality inspection, customs duties, financing costs, and disposal. It prevents sourcing decisions based solely on the lowest quoted price.
details.whyItMatters: The cheapest quoted price often results in the highest total cost after accounting for shipping, quality failures, delays, and administrative overhead.
takeaways: TCO includes all costs from acquisition through use to eventual disposal
Hidden costs like quality failures and shipping often exceed price savings
TCO analysis prevents false economy in low-price sourcing decisions

faq.question: What costs are commonly overlooked in purchasing decisions?
faq.answer: Shipping and customs duties, quality inspection and testing, higher defect rates requiring rework, longer lead times requiring more safety stock, communication overhead across time zones, travel for supplier management, and intellectual property risk from offshore production.

faq.question: How do companies calculate total cost of ownership?
faq.answer: Start with the purchase price, then add all costs to acquire (transport, duties, insurance), use (maintenance, energy, training), and dispose (recycling, decommissioning). Include indirect costs like quality failures, lead time costs, and management overhead.
